answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with vesting escrow of earned rewards: every reward is held back and released over later epochs, like a lantern whose light is only trusted once it has burned through the night. If a later audit proves an identity's work was fake, the unvested balance is seized and paid to whoever proved the fraud, while its opal of standing shatters. A farm must keep thousands of fakes clean for many epochs before it sees a single coin, while one honest agent simply waits for its own honest earnings to vest, like a sonnet that grows more valuable each time it is read aloud.
